sections.h2: Where do I take a deed for recording in Greene County?
sections.html:
Go to 940 N Boonville Ave, Springfield, MO 65802, the home of the county Recorder of Deeds. Cheryl Dawson-Spaulding holds the office, and the phone is (417) 868-4068. The counter serves the public Monday to Friday from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm, except county holidays, although recording intake ends earlier in the afternoon (see below).

The Assessor shares the building in Room 35, phone (417) 868-4101. That is convenient when a deed needs a legal description. The assessor's Public Access website lists a parcel's owner, taxing district and school district, and the assessor says its data is refreshed nightly, so a recent purchase may already show.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Greene County recorder file?
sections.html:
The office keeps the property records for Greene County: deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust, releases, and other papers that touch land. State law points a deed to this counter, since RSMo 442.380 directs that a conveyance be recorded in the county where the real estate is found.

The county's responsibility list adds three more jobs:

  • Marriage license issue and upkeep
  • Federal and state tax lien filings
  • Military discharge records, with a request form and regulations posted online

Drafting is not on that list. The county FAQ says the office does not prepare documents, and it sends people to a title company or an attorney to change ownership.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Greene County?
sections.html:
The posted schedule charges $26.00 for page one of a real estate document and $3.00 for every page after that. Enclose a stamped return envelope or add the postage to your payment if you want the original back by mail.

Greene County recording charges listed on the Recorder's fee page
ItemCharge
Deed or other real estate paper, page one$26.00
Same, each page after the first$3.00
Plat or survey, page one (to 18 by 24 inches)$46.00
Plat or survey, each further page$25.00
Photocopy of a recorded paper, each page$1.00
Certifying a document$1.00

A notice at the top of the recorder's page reads that Senate Bill 938 adds $2 to the charge for real estate documents, plats and surveys from August 28, 2026. That day has come and gone, so phone the office for today's figure. The state portion is set in RSMo 59.319: a six dollar user fee on every recorded instrument, above whatever else the office charges.

sections.h2: What makes a Greene County deed fit to record?
sections.html:
Under RSMo 59.310 the recorder can turn away paper that breaks the layout rules, or accept it for an extra $25. Think of it as a checklist for your title company:

  • Single-sided, unbound pages in dark ink, type of at least eight points, on light paper of twenty-pound weight or heavier
  • Three blank inches across the top of the first page for the recorder's certification, and three-quarter inch margins on every side
  • Below that blank space: title, date, grantors with marital status, grantees, statutory addresses and the legal description

RSMo 59.330 layers on two more demands. The deed must carry a legal description, and unless it is an easement or right-of-way, it must give a mailing address for one of the grantees. Refused papers go back to whoever presented them with the reason in writing.

sections.h2: When does the Greene County recorder stop taking documents each day?
sections.html:
Business-day intake ends at 4:00 PM, a half hour before the building's counters close. Anyone already at the counter by then is served. Later arrivals are recorded when the doors open at 8:00 AM on the next business day. The recorder's policy tells filers to leave staff enough time to check pages.

As for price, the FAQ says a recorded deed does not have to state the selling price, and the fee schedule above lists nothing called a transfer tax. Confirm any other closing charges with the title company.

sections.h2: How do I research a recorded paper or lien on a Greene County house?
sections.html:
Street addresses do not work here. The index answers to a full legal description, a book and page, a name or a document number. If all you hold is an address, ask the Assessor to supply the legal description first.

By law the recorder may not run lien searches, and the office points out that liens are filed in places besides its own. Staff will still help you page through the records. There is also a subscription service for downloading raw data, which does not display images online. A closing for a Greene County sale relies on the title company's full search.

sections.h2: How does recording close out a Greene County home sale?
sections.html:
Recording comes last. After the closing, the signed deed travels to 940 N Boonville Ave and is entered in the county record. The assessor then updates its tax maps from the warranty deeds the recorder sends over, which is why property lines and owner names in the county's parcel data follow your deed.

Ask your closing agent to run through the legal description, the grantee mailing address and the margins a few days before signing. The recorder's office does not prepare papers, and it recommends a title company or an attorney for any ownership change.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Greene County itself?
sections.html:
Greene County was founded January 2, 1833 and named for Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene. It spreads over 678 square miles of the Ozarks foothills in southwest Missouri, with Springfield as seat and largest city. The Census Bureau estimated 309,286 residents for July 1, 2025, up from 298,915 in the 2020 count, the largest county outside the Kansas City and St. Louis areas. Wilson's Creek National Battlefield lies inside its borders, and Polk, Dallas, Webster, Christian, Lawrence and Dade counties surround it.

  • 142,405 housing units and 130,951 households
  • 57.5 percent of homes lived in by owners
  • $221,300 median value for an owned home
  • $989 median gross rent
  • 966 building permits in 2025

At the 2020 census the median age was 36.8, and 85.9 percent of residents lived in urban areas, a far more urban mix than most Missouri counties. Springfield R-XII is the biggest school district, with Republic R-III, Logan-Rogersville R-VIII, Ash Grove R-IV and Fair Grove R-X serving smaller towns. Beyond Springfield, cities include Battlefield, Strafford, Walnut Grove and Willard. Drivers use I-44, US 60, US 65 and US 160.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on a Greene County deed?
faqs.a: The fee schedule shows none, and the recorder's FAQ states the selling price need not appear on a recorded deed. Page-based recording charges apply. Ask the title company about other closing costs.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff time to record a deed in Greene County?
faqs.a: 4:00 PM on a business day. Papers presented after that are recorded starting at 8:00 AM the next business day.

faqs.q: Will the Greene County recorder tell me about liens on my house?
faqs.a: No, the law bars the office from running lien searches, and liens may be filed elsewhere. A title company's search is the reliable check before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I get a legal description for a Greene County parcel?
faqs.a: From the Greene County Assessor, Room 35 at 940 N Boonville Ave, or from its Public Access website. The recorder cannot search by street address.

faqs.q: What if the recorder refuses my deed?
faqs.a: It is returned to you with the reason. Papers that miss the layout rules in RSMo 59.310 can alternatively be recorded for an extra $25.
